name: Northeastern Timbira
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Nimuendaju vocabularies (1914, 1915) and ethnography (1946 Eastern Timbira); no phonological description of Kreye

sources.citation: Nikulin, Andrey. 2020. Proto-Macro-Jê: um estudo reconstrutivo. Tese de doutorado, Universidade de Brasília. 595 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Krẽjê appears only as isolated cited forms (e.g. Krẽjê am-cy 'vespa', fn. 34); Timbira overview (pp. 10-11) covers living varieties only. Remarks that tonic syllables are final in Proto-Cerratense/Proto-Jê de Goyaz ('Em sílabas tônicas (finais)', §4) are reconstructive, not a statement about Krẽjê.

sources.citation: Castro Alves, Flávia de. 2004. O Timbira falado pelos Canela Apãniekrá: uma contribuição aos estudos da morfossintaxe de uma língua Jê. Tese de doutorado, Unicamp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Glottolog's cited basis (with Nimuendajú 1946:6) for the krey1238 grouping; treats Timbira as one language with dialects and states a stress rule for Timbira — would supply at most a second-hand, complex-wide statement, since its data are Apãniekrá [apan1243], not Krẽjê.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú-Unkel, Curt. 1914. Vokabular und Sagen der Crengêz-Indianer (Tajé). Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46: 626-636.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 626 'Orthographie' only defines a diacritic: the acute marks 'daß der Vokal tontragend ist' (that the vowel bears the stress); stress is then marked item by item in the c. 300-word list (Krẽjê of Bacury/Bacabal, Rio Mearim). No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x, languoid krey1238 'Northeastern Timbira' (Hammarström et al.)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic/classificatory only: Glottolog's most extensive description = Nimuendajú 1914 (wordlist or less); subclassification after Nimuendajú 1946:6 and Castro Alves 2004; dialects cuko1234, krej1234, timb1265.

sources.citation: Amado, Rosane de Sá & Souza, Lílian de Carvalho de. 2006. Notas sobre a fonologia da língua timbira. ReVEL 4(7).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists Krenjê among Timbira peoples but states 'O povo Krenjê não fala mais a língua Timbira, somente o Português'; no Krenjê data, no stress statement for it.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt. 1946. The Eastern Timbira (transl. and ed. R. H. Lowie). University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 41. Berkeley/Los Angeles: University of California Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnography. Orthography footnote (p. 1) explains vowel/consonant symbols only; p. 6 gives the dialect classification (Northern group: Timbira of Araparytíua, Krẽyé of Bacabal, Kukóekamekra) that Glottolog's krey1238 follows; p. 17-18 says the Bacabal dialect 'greatly resembles that of the Timbira of Araparytiua'. Nothing on stress placement (only an aside that Northwestern Ge 'would never have lopped off an accented syllable' of a Tupi loan).

sources.citation: Nimuendajú Unkel, Curt. 1915. Vocabulare der Timbiras von Maranhão und Pará. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 47: 302-305.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Four-column comparative word table (I Crengêz 'tájé' of Bacury; II Timbira 'krẽjé' of Bacabá on the Cajuapára; III Timbira 'mehĩ' of Araparytíua, upper Gurupy; IV Canellas). No prose, no orthographic note; diacritics on forms only.
Stub citing only Ethnologue 16 and Glottolog; no phonology.

sources.citation: Ribeiro Silva, Nandra. 2020. Reconstrução fonológica do Proto-Timbira. Tese (Doutorado em Estudos Linguísticos), Instituto de Letras e Comunicação, Universidade Federal do Pará (orient. Ana Vilacy Galúcio).

sources.note: Only modern phonological treatment of the whole Timbira complex; the one place likely to interpret Nimuendajú's Krẽjê/Araparytíua accent marks and to state a stress generalisation (final stress) explicitly covering the extinct northern varieties.
